---
title: "Early Life"
subtitle: "From the Transkei to the law courts of Johannesburg"
---

## Childhood in the Transkei

Nelson Rolihlahla Mandela was born on 18 July 1918 in the village of Mvezo in
the Transkei region of what is now the Eastern Cape, South Africa. He was a
member of the Thembu royal family; his father, Gadla Henry Mphakanyiswa, was
a local chief and counselor to the Thembu king. The name "Rolihlahla"
colloquially means "troublemaker" — a name Mandela later joked was
prophetic.

After his father's death when Mandela was around nine years old, he became a
ward of Jongintaba Dalindyebo, the acting regent of the Thembu people, who
raised him alongside his own children and groomed him for a role advising
the royal house.

## Education

Mandela attended a local mission school, where a teacher gave him the English
name "Nelson," and later Clarkebury Boarding Institute and Healdtown, a
Methodist secondary school. He went on to study at the University of Fort
Hare, one of the few institutions of higher learning open to Black South
Africans at the time, but was expelled for joining a student protest.

He completed his BA degree by correspondence and moved to Johannesburg,
where he studied law at the University of the Witwatersrand. There he met
many future leaders of the anti-apartheid movement across racial lines,
shaping the political outlook that would define the rest of his life.

## Entering Politics

In Johannesburg, Mandela worked as a law clerk and became increasingly
involved in anti-colonial and African nationalist politics. In 1943 he
joined the African National Congress (ANC), and in 1944 he helped found the
ANC Youth League alongside Oliver Tambo, Walter Sisulu, and others, pushing
the ANC toward more assertive, mass-based action against racial
discrimination.

In 1952, Mandela and Tambo opened South Africa's first Black-owned law firm,
Mandela & Tambo, providing free or low-cost legal counsel to Black South
Africans affected by apartheid laws — work that deepened his understanding
of the system he would spend the rest of his life fighting.

::: {.quote-block}
"Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world."
:::
